es: Discrepar con tacto en un diálogo: reconocer lo válido, marcar el contraste con although, matizar tu posición y ofrecer una alternativa o un punto medio.

vocabulary.es: ceder ambos, llegar a un punto medio

teaching.en: You make a fair point about the price, although I see it differently, and my main concern is the choice of venue.
teaching.es: Tienes razón en lo del precio, aunque yo lo veo distinto, y mi principal preocupación es la elección del local.
teaching.explanationEs: a fair point reconoce lo razonable antes de discrepar; although marca el contraste sin añadir but.
segments: You make a fair point about the price, although I see
it differently, and my main concern is the choice of venue.
teaching.audioText: You make a fair point about the price, although I see it differently, and my main concern is the choice of venue.

teaching.en: I understand your concern, but instead of cancelling the dinner, we could move it to Sunday.
teaching.es: Entiendo tu preocupación, pero en lugar de cancelar la cena, podríamos pasarla al domingo.
teaching.explanationEs: concern nombra lo que inquieta al otro; instead of + -ing propone otra acción en lugar de la primera.
segments: I understand your concern, but instead of cancelling
the dinner, we could move it to Sunday.
teaching.audioText: I understand your concern, but instead of cancelling the dinner, we could move it to Sunday.

teaching.en: That is a valid proposal; however, the alternative might be cheaper, and I suspect we will never quite see eye to eye on the cost.
teaching.es: Es una propuesta válida; sin embargo, la alternativa podría ser más barata, y sospecho que nunca nos pondremos del todo de acuerdo en el costo.
teaching.explanationEs: valid reconoce; however marca el contraste; see eye to eye significa coincidir plenamente.
segments: That is a valid proposal; however, the alternative might be cheaper, and I
suspect we will never quite see eye to eye on the cost.
teaching.audioText: That is a valid proposal; however, the alternative might be cheaper, and I suspect we will never quite see eye to eye on the cost.

teaching.en: If you want the park and I want a picnic, we could meet halfway and split the difference, which is a fair compromise.
teaching.es: Si tú quieres el parque y yo un picnic, podríamos ceder los dos y repartir la diferencia, lo cual es un acuerdo justo.
teaching.explanationEs: meet halfway: cada uno cede un poco; split the difference: cada uno asume la mitad de lo que los separa.
segments: If you want the park and I want a picnic, we could
meet halfway and split the difference, which is a fair compromise.
teaching.audioText: If you want the park and I want a picnic, we could meet halfway and split the difference, which is a fair compromise.

teaching.en: Sometimes the most honest result is to agree to differ, but a good negotiator first searches for a middle ground and offers an alternative.
teaching.es: A veces el resultado más honesto es aceptar que se piensa distinto, pero un buen negociador busca primero un terreno intermedio y ofrece una alternativa.
teaching.explanationEs: agree to differ cierra el desacuerdo sin ganador; a middle ground es la posición intermedia que ambos aceptan.
segments: Sometimes the most honest result is to agree to differ, but a
good negotiator first searches for a middle ground and offers an alternative.
teaching.audioText: Sometimes the most honest result is to agree to differ, but a good negotiator first searches for a middle ground and offers an alternative.

teaching.en: My proposal is a compromise that keeps everyone involved, so I suggest we try it for a month and then review it together.
teaching.es: Mi propuesta es un acuerdo que mantiene a todos implicados, así que sugiero probarla durante un mes y revisarla juntos.
teaching.explanationEs: proposal y compromise cierran el desacuerdo con una salida concreta y revisable.
segments: My proposal is a compromise that keeps everyone involved, so I suggest
we try it for a month and then review it together.
teaching.audioText: My proposal is a compromise that keeps everyone involved, so I suggest we try it for a month and then review it together.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tienes razón en lo de la comida, aunque yo lo veo distinto.»

feedback.es: Fair point reconoce lo razonable del otro antes de discrepar.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de «a fair point»: razonable, justo.

origin.text: You make a ___ point about the food, although I see it differently. Still, I am not entirely convinced that a restaurant is the right choice for everyone.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta para ofrecer una alternativa a cancelar la cena.

choices.text: Instead to cancel, we could move the dinner to Tuesday.
Instead cancelling, we could move the dinner to Tuesday.
Instead of cancelling, we could move the dinner to Tuesday.

feedback.es: Instead se une con of y un verbo en -ing: instead of cancelling.

hint.es: Piensa en la preposición que acompaña a instead y en la forma del verbo.

origin.text: Your friend wants to cancel the dinner because the restaurant is closed on Monday. You want to keep the plan and suggest a different day.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Busquemos un punto medio y repartamos la diferencia entre tu idea y la mía.»

answer.text: Let's meet halfway and split the difference between your idea and mine

feedback.es: Meet halfway y split the difference expresan que cada uno cede un poco.

hint.es: Empieza con Let's y termina con el contraste entre dos ideas.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión de la respuesta de Leo evita el error de «although… but»?

choices.text: Although I understand your concern, I think the dinner is too expensive.
Although I understand your concern, but I think the dinner is too expensive.
I understand your concern although, but the dinner is too expensive.

feedback.es: Although ya marca el contraste: no se añade but, como sí se hace en español con «aunque… pero».

origin.text: Leo wants to answer Ana's plan for an expensive dinner politely, and he writes four versions before he sends one of them.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué alternativa propone Mia.

choices.text: Watching the film at home tonight and eating out later.
Going to the film on Saturday afternoon and eating afterwards.
Going tonight, but leaving before the film ends.

feedback.es: Mia reconoce el punto de Tom y propone «instead of going tonight» ir el sábado por la tarde y cenar después.

origin.audio: Tom wanted to watch a film tonight, but Mia was tired. She began by telling him that it was a fair point that the film was about to leave the cinema, although she was not sure she could stay awake. Then she suggested that, instead of going tonight, they could go on Saturday afternoon and have dinner afterwards. Tom thought about it for a moment, smiled, and agreed that it was a good compromise, because it gave each of them something and cost neither of them a whole evening.

prompt.es: Completa cada paso del desacuerdo con la palabra adecuada.

feedback.es: Concern nombra lo que inquieta, meet halfway busca el punto medio y alternative nombra otra opción.

sentences: I understand your ___, but I would like to explain my side.
Let's ___ halfway and choose a day in the middle.
Instead of arguing, we could agree on an ___ plan.

prompt.es: Escribe un diálogo de ocho turnos en el que dos amigos discrepan con tacto.

answer.text: Ana: I think we should celebrate the end of term at the theme park, because everyone enjoys the rides and the day would be unforgettable. Leo: You make a fair point about the rides, although I see it slightly differently, and my main concern is the price of the tickets. Ana: I understand your concern, but the park has a group discount, and I suppose that makes it more reasonable than it looks. Leo: That is a valid point, albeit one I cannot check right now. I'm afraid some of our friends cannot afford even a discounted ticket. Ana: Hmm, I had not thought about that. What do you suggest instead? Leo: How about a picnic by the river, with games and music? It would be cheaper, and everyone could come without worrying about money. Ana: A picnic is an alternative I like, although I wonder whether the weather might spoil it. Perhaps we could have both, on different days? Leo: Let's meet halfway: a picnic on Friday afternoon and, if the group has enough money, the park on Saturday. Does that sound fair?
accepted: Ana: I think we should celebrate the end of term at the theme park, because everyone enjoys the rides and the day would be unforgettable. Leo: You make a fair point about the rides, although I see it slightly differently, and my main concern is the price of the tickets. Ana: I understand your concern, but the park has a group discount, and I suppose that makes it more reasonable than it looks. Leo: That is a valid point, albeit one I cannot check right now. I'm afraid some of our friends cannot afford even a discounted ticket. Ana: Hmm, I had not thought about that. What do you suggest instead? Leo: How about a picnic by the river, with games and music? It would be cheaper, and everyone could come without worrying about money. Ana: A picnic is an alternative I like, although I wonder whether the weather might spoil it. Perhaps we could have both, on different days? Leo: Let's meet halfway: a picnic on Friday afternoon and, if the group has enough money, the park on Saturday. Does that sound fair?

Ana: I would like a big dinner at a restaurant to celebrate the end of term, because the food there is excellent and everybody could sit together. Leo: That is a valid idea, although I am not entirely sure about the cost, and my concern is that some friends might not come. Ana: I understand your concern, but the restaurant offers a fixed price, and I suppose that keeps things under control. Leo: I see your point. However, I wonder whether everyone can pay so much, because a fixed price is still a lot for students. Ana: Perhaps you are right. What do you suggest instead? Leo: How about a dinner at my house? We could cook together, and it would be much cheaper for the whole group. Ana: That sounds fun, although I'm afraid my cooking is not very good. I suppose it is a good compromise, as long as I can choose the dessert. Leo: Great! You choose the dessert, I choose the music, and we split the difference on the cost.

feedback.es: Un buen diálogo reconoce (fair point), marca el contraste (although), matiza (I'm afraid, slightly), ofrece una alternativa (instead, how about) y cierra con un punto medio.

origin.text: Ana y Leo quieren celebrar el fin de curso. Ana prefiere un parque de atracciones y Leo un picnic. Escribe ocho turnos (Ana, Leo, Ana, Leo…) con reconocimiento del punto del otro, concesión, un matiz, una alternativa y un punto medio.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hace Tom para discrepar con tacto de la propuesta de Sara?

choices.text: He acknowledges her reason, names a problem and offers an alternative.
He rejects her reason, but agrees to Friday if she prepares the agenda.
He accepts Friday evening, but asks for a shorter meeting instead.
He says nothing about the day and asks her to choose another one.

feedback.es: Reconoce el motivo de Sara, señala que el viernes por la tarde es difícil y propone el lunes por la mañana, ofreciéndose a preparar la agenda.

origin.text: Sara proposed holding the team meeting on Friday evening. Tom answered that he could see why she wanted to finish the week with a clear plan, but that Friday evening was difficult for most of the team. He wondered whether Monday morning might work instead, and offered to prepare the agenda himself.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ninguno quiere pagar todo, así que repartamos la diferencia.»

feedback.es: Split the difference es la colocación para que cada parte asuma la mitad de lo que las separa.

origin.text: Neither of us wants to pay the full price for the room, so let's split the ___ and each pay half of the extra cost.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Entiendo tu preocupación, pero quizá podríamos encontrar un punto medio.»

answer.text: I see your concern but perhaps we could find a middle ground

feedback.es: Concern reconoce la inquietud del otro y perhaps we could introduce la propuesta de un punto medio.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige cómo reconoce Sara el punto de su amigo.

choices.text: She accepts part of his idea but keeps a doubt.
She rejects his idea in favour of a cheaper one.
She agrees with everything he says about the train.

feedback.es: «Fair point» acepta una parte; «not entirely sure» mantiene la duda, y la pregunta final pide una alternativa sin rechazar el plan.

origin.audio: Sara listened to her friend's plan for the trip. She told him that it was a fair point that the train would be quicker, although she was not entirely sure it would suit everyone, because some of the group could not afford the ticket. She did not reject the plan; she asked whether they could look for something cheaper.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase ofrece la contrapropuesta más diplomática?

choices.text: I take your point, but the restaurant is too expensive, so we must choose another.
I take your point about the food, but how about a smaller place instead?
I am not entirely convinced, so perhaps you should find a cheaper place yourself.

feedback.es: Reconocer el punto de Mia y proponer «how about… instead» mantiene la relación; las otras dos dictan la decisión o pasan la carga a Mia.

origin.text: Mia wants to hold the party at a restaurant, but Leo thinks it is too expensive for some of the guests. He wants to answer without upsetting her, and still suggest a cheaper place.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tras una hora sin convencernos, acordamos no estar de acuerdo.»

feedback.es: Agree to differ es la expresión para cerrar un desacuerdo sin ganador.

origin.text: We talked for an hour without convincing each other, so in the end we decided to agree to ___ and to stay friends.
